subject: Staggered commit & credit bridge — proposal for order form language
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lumerasys.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, sarah.cheng@lumerasys.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Staggered commit / credit bridge options for Lumera order form

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here has reviewed the proposed order form and pricing schedule and we have two items we need to resolve before we can proceed to legal: a) Lumera wants the ability to stagger the commit across three billing quarters (we'd like 40%/30%/30% for the first year) and b) we are asking for a credit-bridge mechanism if usage in Q1 is materially below the first-tier commit.

High-level asks from our side:
- Allow staged commitment (40/30/30) with a capped true-up in month 13.
- If Q1 usage < 60% of the 40% tranche, Lumera requests a one-time credit equal to up to 25% of that tranche (applied to future invoices) rather than an immediate top-up.
- Need explicit caps/floors language so our CFO can model cash flow.

I attached our procurement worksheet with the fill-ins. Can your legal ops provide suggested language that preserves your revenue protections while giving Lumera smoothing options? Also cc'd Sarah (IT security) for visibility — she may have a separate SOC/retention question later.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Procurement, Lumera Systems
Attachments: Lumera_Procurement_Worksheet_v1.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lumerasys.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-03T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staggered commit / credit bridge options for Lumera order form

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks and the worksheet. Short answer: we can work toward a compromise that keeps unit economics predictable for both sides. A couple of notes up front:
- We prefer a true-up model over credits that defer revenue recognition indefinitely; that said, a one-time credit applied to future invoices is workable if capped and timeboxed (we typically accept credits up to 25% of the tranche if spread over the following 2 quarters).
- For staggered commits, we can accept a 40/30/30 split with a 12-month true-up window (month 13 true-up).
- We need clear cap/floor language in the pricing exhibit to avoid unintended clawbacks; proposing a 15% floor per tranche and a hard cap equal to the committed amount.

I'll ask Legal to draft proposed exhibit text and have Marissa pull the order form redline for the 40/30/30 split. Laura — can you take first pass on the exhibit language for the credit-bridge? We want to avoid open-ended credits and ensure the credit reduces invoice liability rather than creates a perpetual credit balance.

Next steps: Jordan to circulate redline + clause suggestion by tomorrow EOD; then Lumera legal/procurement can mark up.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-03T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Order form implications for 40/30/30 split

Jordan / Laura —

Quick internal note on implications if we accept 40/30/30 + credit-bridge:
- Billing cadence: recommend month-by-month billing but with quarterly measurement windows to compute true-ups to limit monthly volatility.
- Accounting: if credit is applied to future invoices we need an explicit expiration (we typically use 6 months post-credit).
- Capacity planning: flag to Ops that initial reserved pool sizing needs a conservative cushion for Q1 (suggest +10% buffer).

I can produce a redline of the order form showing the split and a sample credit worksheet. Ben — please outline the exhibit wording you want legal to review (caps/floors/credit application).

-Marissa
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-04T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed exhibit text (redline attached)

Team —

Draft language below that I put into the exhibit redline (attached as redline_orderform_v2.pdf). Please review and flag if you want the credit framed differently.

--- proposed pricing exhibit snippet ---
1. Staggered Commitment: Customer commits to a Year 1 minimum of N tokens structured as three tranches: 40% (Tranche A), 30% (Tranche B), 30% (Tranche C). Usage will be measured in quarterly windows.
2. True-up: If cumulative usage at month 13 is below the Year 1 minimum, Customer will true-up to the committed amount. True-up payments will be invoiced in the first invoice following month 13.
3. Credit-Bridge Option: If usage in Tranche A (first quarter) is less than sixty percent (60%) of Tranche A, Provider will issue a one-time credit equal to up to twenty-five percent (25%) of the shortfall of Tranche A. Such credit shall: (a) be applied against invoices for the following two (2) billing periods; (b) expire six (6) months after issuance; and (c) shall not affect Provider's right to true-up at month 13.
4. Caps/Floors: Each tranche has a floor of eighty-five percent (85%) of the tranche amount for invoicing purposes and a hard cap equal to 100% of the tranche amount.
5. Accounting/Recognition: Credits issued under section 3 are applied as contra-invoice items and do not change the committed minimum for true-up determination.

--- end snippet ---

Laura — if that read aligns with legal precedent, we can send this to Lumera as line-editable text. Jordan — happy to tweak the cap/floor numbers if you want to be more conservative.

-Ben
Director, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_orderform_v2.pdf
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lumerasys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sarah Cheng <sarah.cheng@lumerasys.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staggered commit / credit bridge options for Lumera order form

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed wording. A few counterpoints from procurement and finance:
- We like the 12-month true-up, but would prefer the credit to be applied over three billing periods (not two) to smooth Q2/Q3 cash flow.
- The 25% cap on the credit is acceptable if the credit application window is 3 invoices and the expiration is 9 months rather than 6.
- We request that the floor be 80% per tranche (instead of 85%) to allow for small seasonal dips without immediate true-up pressure.

I've attached our updated worksheet with calculations reflecting the 3-period credit application and 9-month expiration (Lumera_Procurement_worksheet_filled.xlsx). Also note that Lumera's legal has asked for a simple definition of "shortfall" to avoid ambiguous measurement.

If you can accept these three small changes, I think procurement and legal can greenlight the order form and move to signature.

Best,
Tom
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@lumerasys.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-06T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Staggered commit / credit bridge options for Lumera order form — compromise

Tom —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity and the updated worksheet. We can accept Lumera's requested tweaks with the following conditions so the economics are protected and legal has clean language:
- Credit application: extend to three (3) billing periods and expiration to nine (9) months (accepted).
- Floor: adjust to 80% per tranche (accepted).
- Definition of "shortfall": replace with a specific formula in the exhibit: "Shortfall = max(0, TrancheAmount - RecordedUsageDuringTrancheWindow). RecordedUsageDuringTrancheWindow means the sum of billed usage tokens during the tranche's measurement window as recorded in Provider's billing system."

We will update the redline PDF and the exhibit snippet to reflect those changes and circulate a final version for Lumera legal's line edits by EOD Friday. Action items:
- Jordan to send updated redline + exhibit (Ben/Marissa) — EOD 2026-11-06.
- Lumera to review with legal and confirm sign-off by 2026-11-10 if possible.
- Laura to confirm there are no additional compliance hooks (e.g., reporting cadence) for the credit event.

Assuming agreement, next step will be a DocuSign-ready order form.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
